scope: Independent static review only; no device, SDK, build or additional tests

findings.issue: Loaded note hashes and disk module metadata are only recorded independently. A disk r0 hash does not establish that the currently loaded module is r0.
findings.minimal_fix: For hci_uart, btqca and btbcm, record loaded presence/initstate plus compare sysfs .note.gnu.build-id bytes or their hash with the note section of the verified current k363 ELF. Reuse kernel234/collect-baseline.py note() or package-hardening hardening.elf_sections(). Treat a missing note on a present module as unknown/failure, not unloaded. Include the comparison in the public status booleans without exposing identities.

findings.issue: The owner check and default proxy for the well-known org.bluez name are separate operations. If BlueZ exits between them, the proxy/introspection or later default method call may activate the service.
findings.minimal_fix: Resolve GetNameOwner once, use that unique bus name with introspect=False, and call GetManagedObjects with an explicit timeout. A vanished unique owner should yield an unavailable inventory, without activating a replacement service.

findings.issue: The outer SSH timeout is 100 seconds, but many independent remote commands each allow 20 seconds and the D-Bus call uses its implicit default timeout. Their aggregate allowance exceeds the transport budget. A transport timeout loses the final JSON and does not prove that the remote reader has ended.
findings.minimal_fix: Bound the remote inventory as a whole within the transport budget, give D-Bus an explicit timeout, and retain partial command-status evidence on timeout. Do not replay a stateful transaction or infer idle from a missing final receipt.

findings.issue: A failed D-Bus inventory currently summarizes as zero adapters, zero paired and zero connected devices, while no_device_changes remains true. Those zeros are not evidence that Bluetooth is idle.
findings.minimal_fix: Keep the script as an inventory, but explicitly report D-Bus/MGMT probe validity and use unknown/null counts on missing inventory. Any later deployment gate must require valid probes, or independently establish stopped bluetoothd and absent hci_uart/controller after the explicit stop operation.

findings.issue: Only **/info is hashed. This can establish stability of those device files, but does not justify claiming that the entire /var/lib/bluetooth state or all local identity data is preserved.
findings.minimal_fix: For the deployment transaction, privately snapshot the existing Bluetooth storage files with relative paths, hashes and permissions, including adapter settings/identity files when present. Compare only relevant unchanged state after the test; preserve the original info files and key sections. Do not delete existing paired devices or overwrite their state with an older generic backup.

findings.issue: The adopted boot guard is checked in a separate SSH command from the requested operation. This is useful for read-only inspection but leaves a boot-change gap before future mutations.
findings.minimal_fix: Retain the original authenticated transport/adoption. For a future state change, perform the current boot/release check inside the same native transaction immediately before mutation, and record boot ID again at completion. A newly reported boot requires a fresh adoption, not silent reuse of kernel449 guard state.

handoff: Charging owner explicitly confirms its worker ended and returns the device window; USB recovery uncertainty must be resolved first.
No new system suspend, reboot, USB reprobe or charging service/module action is included in the Bluetooth window.
before_stop: Current adopted boot ID and exact k363 release; taint and only relevant new kernel errors.
Canonical paths, actual APK owners, exact byte hashes and loaded-note matches for hci_uart, btqca and btbcm against r0/k363.
BlueZ owner/PID and valid adapter state: Powered, Discovering, Pairable, Discoverable plus valid connected-device count; no pending samurai-bluetooth lifecycle lock/worker.
Private Bluetooth storage/config snapshot, original service enable/running state, and hash of the unchanged helper/address-assistant bytes.
Current charging manifest equals the handed-off manifest; only read its existing limits/protection state. Preserve camera440 and existing charging/USB module identity.
immediately_before_r2_install: Explicitly stop BlueZ and use the existing Bluetooth helper stop order; do not force unload or remove a stale lifecycle lock.
Confirm bluetoothd absent, hci_uart absent and hci0 unregistered; no other owner is using the Bluetooth window.
Confirm all three disk modules still match r0 and package ownership permits the intended signed package transition. Do not bypass unrelated owners with force-overwrite.
Verify r2 APK signature and exact hci_uart candidate SHA fe14136068584d212625a7c2bfb20b72e082539daa10dfcecd877e43531fc32d.
after_start_and_cleanup: Use the existing helper/address setup and standard service only; loaded hci_uart note must match r2 ELF, unchanged btqca/btbcm notes must match their baseline ELFs.
First verify ordinary controller setup and the chosen bounded Bluetooth action; retain separate failed results. Do not add system PM while SDP/USB recovery is unresolved.
Return to the original adapter/service state, disconnect only the test peer, stop only discovery owned by the test, and compare original key/config state.
Same boot, charging manifest/protection identity and camera payload; no camera test or charging writes are needed for this module change.

rollback_transaction_requirement: Save verified original r0 module bytes and ownership/version evidence before installing r2; retain signed r0 and r2 APKs.
On rollback, inspect current state rather than replaying the deployment worker. Stop BlueZ and unload the Bluetooth modules using the same guarded order; confirm hci_uart/controller absence.
The existing r0 adoption hook rejects r2 bytes. Therefore restoring the original r0 file and the package-database downgrade must be an explicit reviewed transaction, not a blind apk add of r0.

After restoring the exact r0 bytes and consistent package ownership/version, reload normally and compare loaded ELF notes, keys, config and original idle/service state. Saving an r0 APK alone is not a tested runtime rollback.
not_required_for_this_change: Camera captures, audio route changes, modem restarts
Charging/USB service restart, module replacement or limit writes
New Image/DTB build, flash or system suspend
